## How much cake does each student receive? {#ss7-cake-totals .lim-lesson }

The new pieces are $\dfrac13,\ \dfrac19,\ \dfrac1{27},\ldots$

**Predict:** how much cake will each student receive if this continues?

::: {.fragment data-fragment-index="0"}

$$S_1=\frac13,\qquad S_2=\frac49,\qquad S_3=\frac{13}{27}$$

:::

::: {.fragment data-fragment-index="1"}

After $n$ rounds, Mr Greasley has $\left(\dfrac13\right)^n$ of the cake left.

$$S_n=\frac{1-\left(\frac13\right)^n}{2}$$

:::

::: {.takeaway .fragment data-fragment-index="2"}

$$\frac13+\frac19+\frac1{27}+\cdots=\frac12$$

:::

::: notes

Invite a prediction and explanation before revealing any totals. Click 1 gives the first three totals for one student. Click 2 uses conservation of the cake: both students share equally what is no longer held by Mr Greasley, so 2S_n+3^(−n)=1. This obtains S_n geometrically before the general formula. Click 3 gives the limiting sum. Every finite total is strictly below one half. Each student eventually receives one half only in the ideal infinite-process sense. An actual cake cannot be divided indefinitely. Ask whether the teacher’s share equals zero after any finite number of cuts.

:::
